Τεμέση , ἡ, a place whence (acc. to Od. 1.184 ) the Taphians obtained copper in exchange for iron: some identified it with Temesa in Bruttium; others read Ταμασόν or Τάμασιν, i.e. Tamassos in Cyprus, v.
Str. 6.1.5 , Paus. 6.6.8 , St.Byz. : ὁ ἐν Τεμέσῃ ἥρως, prov. of misplaced rage, Eust. 1409.14 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
